subject: History
context: Choose the correct option from the given options and complete the sentences.
stem: The earliest museum in the world was discovered in the excavations at the city of ____.
solution: Ur. The world's earliest known museum was found during the excavations of Ur, an ancient city of Mesopotamia (present-day Iraq). The collection of old and carefully labelled objects gathered there by the Babylonian princess Ennigaldi-Nanna is regarded as the first museum. Delhi, Harappa and Kolkata are not associated with the earliest museum.

subject: History
context: Choose the correct option from the given options and complete the sentences.
stem: In Maharashtra, ____ is supposed to be the first Keertankar.
solution: Saint Namdev. Sant Namdev is regarded as the first Keertankar (performer of Keertan) of Maharashtra; he spread the Bhakti tradition through Keertan, a devotional performing art that combines narration, singing and music. Sant Dnyaneshwar, Sant Eknath and Sant Tukaram came later in the same Varkari tradition.

subject: History
context: Choose the correct option from the given options and complete the sentences.
stem: It may be said that ____ was the founder of modern historiography.
solution: Voltaire. The prescribed Balbharati Std-10 History textbook says so outright in Chapter 1 (Historiography: Development in the West): Voltaire held that social traditions, trade, economy and agriculture mattered alongside objective truth and chronology, and 'Thus, it is said that Voltaire was the founder of modern historiography.' This question is reproduced word-for-word from that chapter's own exercise. Descartes insisted on verifying documents critically; Ranke gave the critical original-document method; Marx contributed the class-struggle reading.

subject: History
context: Identify and write the wrong pair in the following sets.
stem:
Identify and write the wrong pair in the following set of newspaper-and-editor pairs:
(i) 'Prabhakar' — Acharya P.K. Atre
(ii) 'Darpan' — Balshastri Jambhekar
(iii) 'Deenbandhu' — Krishnarao Bhalekar
(iv) 'Kesari' — Bal Gangadhar Tilak
solution: The wrong pair is (i) 'Prabhakar' — Acharya P.K. Atre. 'Prabhakar' was started by Bhau Mahajan (Govind Vitthal Kunte); it was in 'Prabhakar' that Lokahitawadi Gopal Hari Deshmukh wrote his 'Shatapatre'. Acharya P.K. Atre's newspaper was 'Maratha'. The other three pairs are correct: 'Darpan' (the first Marathi newspaper, 1832) was started by Balshastri Jambhekar, 'Deenbandhu' by Krishnarao Bhalekar of the Satyashodhak movement, and 'Kesari' by Bal Gangadhar Tilak.

subject: History
context: Identify and write the wrong pair in the following sets.
stem:
Identify and write the wrong pair in the following set of sportsperson-and-sport pairs:
(i) Balambhat Deodhar — Mallakhamb
(ii) Khashaba Jadhav — Football
(iii) Major Dhyan Chand — Hockey
(iv) Sachin Tendulkar — Cricket
solution: The wrong pair is (ii) Khashaba Jadhav — Football. Khashaba Jadhav was a WRESTLER; he won a bronze medal in wrestling at the Helsinki Olympics of 1952 and was the first Indian to win an individual Olympic medal. The correct pair is therefore 'Khashaba Jadhav — Wrestling'. The other three are correct: Balambhat Dada Deodhar revived and developed the traditional sport of Mallakhamb, Major Dhyan Chand was the legendary hockey player, and Sachin Tendulkar is a cricketer.

subject: History
subtopic: Applied History and Research in Various Fields
context: Identify and write the wrong pair in the following sets.
stem:
Identify and write the wrong pair in the following set of university-and-city pairs:
(i) Maharaja Sayajirao University — Delhi
(ii) Banaras Hindu University — Varanasi
(iii) Aligarh Muslim University — Aligarh
(iv) Jivaji University — Gwalior
solution: The wrong pair is (i) Maharaja Sayajirao University — Delhi. The Maharaja Sayajirao University is at VADODARA (Baroda) in Gujarat, not Delhi; it is one of the well-known Indian universities offering courses in archaeology and ancient Indian history. The other three pairs are correct: Banaras Hindu University is at Varanasi (Uttar Pradesh), Aligarh Muslim University at Aligarh (Uttar Pradesh) and Jivaji University at Gwalior (Madhya Pradesh).

subject: History
stem:
Complete the time line related to Television. The printed time line has four marked points; above the line the YEAR is shown and below the line the EVENT is shown. As printed:
Point 1 — year: blank box; event: 'Inauguration of the Delhi Doordarshan'
Point 2 — year: 1972; event: blank box
Point 3 — year: blank box; event: 'Colour television was introduced'
Point 4 — year: 1991; event: blank box
Fill in the four blank boxes.
solution:
The completed time line is:

| Year | Event |
|---|---|
| 1959 | Inauguration of the Delhi Doordarshan (television broadcasting began in India from Delhi) |
| 1972 | The second centre of Doordarshan was started at Mumbai (Bombay), and television spread beyond Delhi |
| 1982 | Colour television was introduced (during the Asian Games held in Delhi) |
| 1991 | Indian television was opened up to private satellite channels, and foreign channels began broadcasting in India |

So the four blanks are: 1959, 'the second Doordarshan centre started at Mumbai', 1982, and 'private satellite channels began in India'.

subject: History
subtopic: Management of Cultural and Natural Heritage
stem: Complete the following tree diagram. As printed, the top box reads 'Cultural Heritage'. It branches into two boxes: 'Tangible' on the left and 'Intangible' on the right. Under EACH of these two boxes there are two blank slots numbered (1) and (2). Fill in the four blank slots with suitable examples.
solution:
Completed tree diagram:

Cultural Heritage

| Tangible | Intangible |
|---|---|
| (1) Forts, temples, caves and other historical monuments (e.g. Ajanta-Ellora caves, Raigad fort) | (1) Folk arts and performing arts — music, dance, theatre such as Powada, Lavani, Keertan and Tamasha |
| (2) Sculptures, paintings, coins, manuscripts, inscriptions and other objects preserved in museums | (2) Languages, literature, festivals, customs, rituals and traditional knowledge and skills |

Tangible heritage is heritage that has a physical, material form and can be seen and touched, while intangible heritage consists of the traditions, skills and expressions handed down from one generation to the next.

subject: History
stem: Write a short note on: Nationalistic Historiography.
solution: Nationalistic historiography is the writing of history from the point of view of one's own nation, with the aim of awakening national pride and self-respect. It arose in India as a reply to the colonial and imperialist historians, who portrayed Indian history as a record of backwardness and justified British rule. Nationalist historians used original sources to show the greatness of India's ancient and medieval past, the achievements of Indian rulers and the exploitative nature of colonial rule. Vishnushastri Chiplunkar, Justice Mahadev Govind Ranade, Vasudev Shastri Khare, Rajwade and Jadunath Sarkar are important names in this tradition; Ranade's writing on the rise of the Maratha power and the studies of the 1857 struggle as India's first war of independence are typical examples. This historiography inspired the freedom movement, though its excessive glorification of the past is also seen as its limitation.

subject: History
stem: Write a short note on: Applied History.
solution: Applied History is the branch of history in which the knowledge of the past is deliberately used for present-day, practical purposes. It does not stop at studying and writing about the past; it makes that knowledge useful to the general public and to society. Applied History is used to conserve and manage historical monuments, forts, caves and other heritage sites, to run museums, archives and libraries, and to plan heritage walks and tourism. It also helps other fields — town planning, archaeology, art, literature, films and serials, advertising, and even administration and law — by supplying reliable information about the past. Because of Applied History, many professional opportunities are available today, such as archaeologist, museologist, archivist, conservator, tour guide and heritage manager. In short, Applied History links the past with the present and makes history a living and useful subject.

subject: History
stem: Write a short note on: Marco Polo.
solution: Marco Polo was a famous traveller and merchant of the thirteenth century who belonged to Venice in Italy. Along with his father and uncle he travelled overland through Persia and Central Asia to China, and stayed for many years at the court of the Mongol emperor Kublai Khan, who employed him on missions in his empire. On his return journey he also travelled by sea and visited the coastal regions of South-East Asia and India. The record of his travels, known as 'The Travels of Marco Polo', gives detailed descriptions of the cities, trade, customs, products and rulers of the lands he saw. His account made the wealth and civilisation of the East known to Europe, encouraged later European explorers, and remains an important source for the history and geography of the period.
